description: Implement a real 3-state (closed/open/half-open) circuit breaker driven via a stdin command protocol, in place of always calling through
prompts: Create a C program in breaker.c implementing a 3-state circuit breaker, driven by commands from stdin (one per line) until EOF: `init FAILURE_THRESHOLD RESET_TIMEOUT` (both ints) initializes it, starting CLOSED. `call OUTCOME NOW` (OUTCOME is the literal string `ok` or `fail`; NOW is an int, seconds) simulates one call attempt: in CLOSED, the call runs for real - print `ran:ok` or `ran:fail`; count consecutive fails, and once FAILURE_THRESHOLD consecutive fails have happened, trip OPEN (record when). While OPEN, a call must NOT run at all - print `blocked` - UNLESS at least RESET_TIMEOUT seconds have passed since it opened, in which case allow exactly ONE trial call (print `ran:ok` or `ran:fail` for it): success closes the breaker (reset fail count); failure re-opens it AND resets the open-time to NOW (so the next trial needs another full RESET_TIMEOUT).
name: add_c_circuit_breaker_state_machine

test_setup_files.test_breaker.py:
import subprocess
subprocess.run(['gcc', '-std=c11', '-Wall', 'breaker.c', '-o', 'breaker_bin'], check=True)

def run(commands):
    text = '\n'.join(commands) + '\n'
    proc = subprocess.run(['./breaker_bin'], input=text, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
    assert proc.returncode == 0, f'nonzero exit: {proc.returncode}, stderr={proc.stderr[-400:]}'
    return [l.strip() for l in proc.stdout.strip('\n').split('\n') if proc.stdout.strip('\n')]

# trips open after consecutive failures, then blocks
out = run(['init 3 10', 'call fail 0', 'call fail 0', 'call fail 0', 'call ok 0'])
assert out == ['ran:fail', 'ran:fail', 'ran:fail', 'blocked'], f'got {out}'

# half-open trial success closes
out = run(['init 1 10', 'call fail 0', 'call ok 10', 'call ok 11'])
assert out == ['ran:fail', 'ran:ok', 'ran:ok'], f'got {out}'

# half-open failure reopens and resets clock
out = run(['init 1 10', 'call fail 0', 'call fail 10', 'call ok 15', 'call ok 20'])
assert out == ['ran:fail', 'ran:fail', 'blocked', 'ran:ok'], f'got {out}'

print('PASS')
